When carrying luggage, you should have instructed Zhan Xing to guard it, and only sent him on other errands after you arrived at the boat; even if he boarded the wrong boat, nothing would have been lost. Now that this has happened, it is simply your fate to lose the money—how can you blame the servant?" They were both released without further depositions.

paragraphs.zh: 按：货物上船，须不离人看守。要防舵公侵盗，又要得智仆为吉也。故雏仆之挑行节，银物所系，须跟在身边，托在实落，方无所失。若先令挑去，错寄别船，安能无失哉？然麟徒知叙旧之谈，致仆误丧其财而干讼者，何其愚也！诸商鉴此，可为后戒。
paragraphs.en: Note: When goods are loaded onto a boat, they must never be left unattended. One must guard against the helmsman stealing and also ensure a clever servant is present for good fortune. Thus, when an inexperienced servant carries the travel bundle—the very thing that holds the silver and goods—he must stay by your side, and you must entrust it only to a reliable place; then nothing will be lost. If you first order him to carry it ahead and it is mistakenly left on another boat, how can there be no loss? Yet Menglin knew only how to reminisce about old times, causing his servant to lose the money by mistake and dragging them into a lawsuit—how foolish! All merchants should take this as a warning.

stories.title_en: A Porter Dashes Off with Unloaded Cargo

paragraphs.zh: 建城溪边，凡客船到岸，众脚夫丛集，求雇担代挑入城。有老成客，必喝退众夫，待船货齐收上岸，都数纪定，然后分作几担，叫几名脚夫，自相识认，乃发入城，急令人跟行其后，方保无失。若雏家到，众脚夫不管物件检齐否，即为收拾上担，及急跟夫去，多致遗物在船中未尽收。
paragraphs.en: By the creek at Jianning city, whenever a merchant boat reaches shore, porters swarm and beg to be hired to carry loads into the city. An experienced traveler will always shout the crowd of porters back, wait until the boat's goods are all brought ashore and counted and recorded, then divide them into several loads, call several porters he can recognize, send them into the city, and at once have someone follow behind; only then is there no loss. If a greenhorn arrives, the porters, without waiting to see whether the things have been fully checked, load them onto the carriers at once; and if you hurry after the porters, you often leave things still on the boat not yet brought in.

paragraphs.zh: 有侯官县一田秀才，出外作馆。年冬归，得束金四十餘两，衣被物件亦十餘两，共作两大笼。经过建城，欲入拜乡亲，命一脚夫挑笼先行。田乃儒家，从后缓步随之。脚夫见其来迟，一步紧一步，趱入城门；人闹攘处，更是疾行，遂挑入曲巷逃走。田从后虽叫“止步”，哪能止得！入城曲巷多歧，何处可寻？次日，往府吕巡捕呈之。
paragraphs.en: There was a licentiate named Tian from Houguan County who went out to tutor. At year's end he returned home with more than forty taels of teaching silver and another ten-odd taels worth of clothes and bedding, packed into two large baskets. Passing through Jiancheng, he wished to enter and visit a fellow townsman, so he ordered a porter to carry the baskets ahead. As a Confucian scholar, Tian followed slowly behind. The porter, seeing him lagging, walked faster and faster, hurried into the city gate; in the crowded throng, he moved even quicker, carrying the load into a winding alley and fled. Though Tian called from behind, "Stop!" how could he stop him? Inside the city, the winding alleys forked many ways—where could one search? The next day, he presented the matter to Prefectural Constable Lü.

paragraphs.zh: 吕捕衙是精明官，以脚扶拐物，须用脚夫查之。即叫二差人来：“你认定这田相公，今午后穿白长衫在船中。行李到，必有脚夫挑走，你二人从后密跟，到他家拿来。”再对秀才曰：“你今再讨假行李一担，在十里外搭船来府，照前日到岸时，叫脚夫来挑。你穿白长衫去，此两差人易认。若已在旁，你故意缓行，任此脚夫挑去，必能拿得前脚夫来。”秀才未会其意。
paragraphs.en: Constable Lü was a sharp official. To catch a porter who had cheated out of goods, you must use porters to find him. He at once called two runners: "You mark this Licentiate Tian. This afternoon he will wear a white long gown on a boat. When luggage arrives, a porter will surely make off with it; you two follow secretly behind and seize him at his house." He then said to the licentiate: "Today get a dummy load of luggage, board a boat ten li out, and come to the prefecture. When you reach shore as you did the other day, call a porter to carry it. Wear a white long gown so these two runners can recognize you. If they are already beside you, walk slowly on purpose and let this porter carry it off; they will surely catch the earlier porter." The licentiate did not yet see his meaning.

paragraphs.zh: 即日下午，备行李从十里外搭船到，见此两美人在旁，各相认得，故叫脚夫挑行李，从后缓随。脚夫果然挑走。二公差迤跟到家拿住，曰：“吕爷叫你。”脚夫黄三不知来历，只得随往。吕爷曰：“你缘何挑走秀才行李？”黄三惊曰：“只暂寄我家，便欲送还。”官止喝：“打五板！”田秀才方到衙。吕爷叮咛黄三曰：“今日饶你罪。这田相公昨日被脚夫挑走一担笼，限你两日代根究来；若寻不出，定坐你赔。”黄三曰：“河下挑夫，两日换一班。昨日不是我辈。”吕爷曰：“你即根究昨日的。”
paragraphs.en: That same afternoon, he packed his luggage, took a boat from ten li away, and arrived. Seeing the two runners beside him, each recognized the other, so he called a porter to carry the luggage and followed slowly behind. The porter indeed made off with it. The two runners trailed him to his house and caught him, saying: "Constable Lü wants you." The porter, Huang San, unaware of the situation, had no choice but to go along. Constable Lü asked: "Why did you run off with the licentiate's luggage?" Startled, Huang San replied: "I only left it at my house temporarily and intended to return it." The official shouted, "Beat him five strokes!" Licentiate Tian then arrived at the yamen. Constable Lü instructed Huang San: "Today I spare your punishment. Yesterday a porter stole one load of Master Tian's goods. You have two days to track him down; if you cannot find him, you will be held liable for the loss." Huang San said: "River porters change shifts every two days. Yesterday was not our shift." Constable Lü replied: "Then you must investigate yesterday's men."

paragraphs.zh: 黄三密访两日，不能得。第三日，公差来拿。到半途，见一脚夫柳五，将银三钱换钱用，随即买鱼肉等归家。黄三再拿到衙，禀曰：“并访不得。只今遇柳五换钱，多买鱼肉，事有可疑。”捕衙立差四人，同田秀才、黄三直往柳五家搜。只一间小房，搜果见赃。拿到捕衙，柳五供曰：“银物现在。前五日未敢出门，今日止用银三钱换钱，买物作欢。拐盗是实。”捕衙发打二十板，曰：“你二脚夫拐资客货，各该拟徒。但黄三捕出柳五，以此赎罪，再打十板释放，以惩后日。姑念柳五穷汉，只拟不应罪，纳完发放。”再叫田秀才具领状来，尽将原物领去。不数日，拿得真赃正犯，非有治才，安能如此哉！
paragraphs.en: Huang San conducted a secret investigation for two days but found nothing. On the third day, officials arrived to arrest him. Halfway there, he spotted a porter named Liu Wu exchanging three qian of silver for cash, then immediately buying fish, meat, and other items to take home. Huang San had Liu Wu seized and brought to the yamen, reporting: "I found nothing during my search. However, I just encountered Liu Wu changing money and purchasing a large quantity of fish and meat; this behavior seems suspicious." The constable promptly dispatched four men, who accompanied Licentiate Tian and Huang San directly to Liu Wu's house to search. They found only a small room, but upon searching, they indeed discovered the stolen goods. Liu Wu was taken to the constable's yamen, where he confessed: "The silver and goods are here. For the past five days, I dared not leave home. Today, I merely used three qian of silver to exchange for cash and buy provisions to celebrate. Yes, I committed the crime of abduction and theft." The constable ordered twenty strokes and declared: "Both of you porters stole a traveler's belongings; each should be sentenced to penal servitude. However, since Huang San caught Liu Wu, his involvement is redeemed. Give him ten additional strokes and release him as a warning for future cases. Considering Liu Wu is a poor man, I will sentence him only for committing an improper act. Once the fine is paid, he may go free." He then instructed Licentiate Tian to submit a receipt, after which all the original goods were returned to him. Within a few days, the true thief and the genuine loot were apprehended. Without exceptional administrative talent, how could such a result have been achieved?

paragraphs.zh: 按：脚夫挑走货物，处处有之，故出行最宜慎防。若吕捕衙之发奸得捕盗不遗余力者，全在以脚夫查脚夫一着。所谓“以蛮夷攻蛮夷”是也。又谚云“贼拿贼，针挑刺”，亦此意也。雇夫者可以为戒，捕盗者可以为法。
paragraphs.en: Note: Porters running off with goods happen everywhere, so travelers must be most vigilant. As for Constable Lü, who uncovered the deceit and captured the thief without sparing any effort, the whole matter hinged on one move: using a porter to catch a porter. This is what is meant by "using barbarians to fight barbarians." The proverb also says, "A thief catches a thief; use a needle to pick out a splinter"—the same idea. Those who hire porters should take this as a warning; those who hunt thieves may take it as a model.
